item.title: Why Antigravity Eats Weekly Quota Fast - and What I Measured
item.author: asubedi@asubedi.com.np (Ashish Subedi)
item.description:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Gemini 4 Argon, and hy4-flash via OpenCode used for the binary reverse engineering, empirical cache probing, and keep-alive tooling.

Introduction

Greetings! If you use Google Antigravity (agy) with the big frontier models, you have probably noticed how fast your weekly quota disappears during normal coding sessions [1, 4].

My suspicion was simple: a short prompt-cache lifetime. When you are coding with an agent, you don’t send messages every 10 seconds. You wait for a response, read the diff, run a test, think for 5 minutes, and then send your next prompt. If the prompt cache expires during that 5-minute pause, your next message has to re-ingest the entire conversation history at full price.

item.title: Reverse Engineering OP Nord Buds 2 with AI
item.author: asubedi@asubedi.com.np (Ashish Subedi)
item.description:
Muse Spark 1.3 used for the reverse engineering process and help with the blog

One thing before we start. I saw that Muse Spark 1.3 had launched with crazy benchmaxx, and it was free to use through opencode. I decided to test it on this genuinely messy reverse engineering task with no existing documentation.

Why bother

I use OnePlus Nord Buds 2 which works great with my Android device. The problem is I sometimes forget to charge it. It’s quite visible in my phone. I also use it with my macbook, but the battery information is not present. I put a small SwiftBar plugin in the menu bar that shows the buds’ battery.
